_note: The government's programme. Every few months (CONFIG.laws) the government tables one of these: the ruling party if it agrees with the law's side (its position past CONFIG.laws.agree), else a partner. It opens a major debate (lines in debate_lines.json TOPIC_LINES under "law_<id>"); after voteMonths parliament votes. A partner on the other side, the public argument going against it, or a weak government can sink it. Fields: axis and side (L/R: which way the law pushes), title, text (what it does), tabled (news when it is tabled; {short} {leader}), minMonth, weight and when (as events), passed {text, world: a jolt now, lasting: where the country's numbers settle from now on}, failed (news text), seeds (events that follow a passed law, months [from, to]; write them in content.json EVENTS with "deck": false).

LAWS.title: The Border Security Bill
LAWS.text: Two thousand new border guards and a fence along the Dillihan frontier, paid for out of the regional development fund.
LAWS.tabled: {short} says the country must "know who is coming in".

passed.text: The fence goes up in sections from the spring. Dillihan recalls its ambassador "for consultations", and the border provinces lose a year of road money.

LAWS.failed: Backbenchers from the border provinces vote against losing their road money. The fence stays a drawing.

LAWS.title: The Public Order Act
LAWS.text: The police may ban a demonstration with a day's notice, and fine the organisers if it goes ahead.
LAWS.tabled: {short} says shopkeepers "have swept up enough glass".

passed.text: From next month a march needs the police's blessing. The first bans are expected within weeks.

LAWS.failed: Enough members of the government vote with the opposition to send the act back. The interior minister calls it "a delay".

LAWS.title: The Family Allowance Act
LAWS.text: A tax credit of ₱250 a month for married couples with children under sixteen.
LAWS.tabled: {short} calls it "a thank-you to the families who hold this country together".

passed.text: The first credits arrive in the autumn. Accountants report a small boom in weddings.

LAWS.failed: The government's own partners vote it down unless every child is covered. The bill goes back to committee and stays there.

LAWS.title: The Bread and Fuel Price Cap
LAWS.text: For two years, the price of bread, cooking gas and heating oil may not rise faster than wages.
LAWS.tabled: {short} says families "cannot wait for the market to feel sorry for them".

passed.text: Prices on the shelves are frozen from Monday. Suppliers warn of "difficulties".

LAWS.failed: The senior party in government lets the cap fall on a technicality. The suppliers' association sends flowers to nobody in particular.

LAWS.title: The Defence Modernisation Act
LAWS.text: Thirty-six new fighter jets from the Bordon Federation over ten years, for ₱4 billion.
LAWS.tabled: {short} says the air force "flies planes older than its pilots".

passed.text: The first two jets arrive next year. The factory that will service them is in Bayernal.

LAWS.failed: The coalition partner refuses to vote for jets while hospitals wait. The order is "postponed".

LAWS.title: The Winter Pension Bonus
LAWS.text: ₱600 for every pensioner, paid each December.
LAWS.tabled: {short} says no pensioner should "spend the winter in a coat indoors".

passed.text: The first bonus is paid this December. Post offices brace for queues.

LAWS.failed: The finance minister's party votes it down as "unaffordable this year". Pensioners' groups promise to remember.
